Definition: from G1537 and G4154; to expire:--give up the ghost.
BiblicalUsage: ekpnéō is a plain word for give up the ghost. In Mark 15:37, the text says "and gave up the ghost." In Mark 15:39, the text says "and gave up the ghost."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, ekpnéō is a reminder that death is real, but it is not the end — God has the last word over it. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
